findings.summary: The cap branch still takes precedence over the blocked downgrade, and C8c now cements it: blocked>0 together with a cap hit reports 'capped', while spec §3.2 literally reads 「只能是『部分完成』」. I accept this as within spec because §3.2's ⛔ constraint is that the state must never be 'converged', and that holds structurally — 'converged' is reachable only through the else-branch where blocked === 0 — while 'capped' equally disclaims completeness per §3.1. No acceptance row adjudicates the overlap: C8 and C9 both construct condition-1 scenarios far below maxClues/maxDepth and both pass. Residual cost is only labeling: an all-blocked board that coincidentally reaches maxClues reads as budget truncation rather than failure.

The drain gate is applied to condition 2 (count cap) as well as condition 3, although spec §3 line 37 scopes 「只拦新 clue，已 open 的跑完」 to condition 3 only; C7d asserts this extension. A side effect is that while capHit is true and an open card remains, condition 1 is never evaluated (else-if), so a board satisfying condition 1 does not stop until it drains and then reports 'capped' rather than 'converged'/'partial', which is a deviation from 「任一满足即停」. Both effects err in the safe direction — more work completed, and an honest cap label rather than a completeness claim — and termination still holds: open cards resolve to explored/blocked, so the 「explored+dropped+blocked」 metric of §4 rises monotonically to the maxClues bound and drained is eventually reached.

C14 (npm run typecheck and npm test both exit 0) is evidenced only by self-report in IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md §四; the sole committed acceptance record carries development_id dev_ledr_s2_tick_01 and a 42-test run predating test/s3.test.ts, so it does not evidence this package. Informational — the acceptance stage regenerates it, and static review found nothing that would fail either command: tsconfig is strict over [src, test], the new required TickConfig fields (maxClues, zeroGrowthThreshold) break no existing literal because test/tick.test.ts derives cfg from DEFAULT_TICK_CONFIG, and every decideTermination call site in test/s3.test.ts supplies all four TerminationInput fields.

Spec §7's proof that the tightened B1 guard actually bites, and §8's P6 row, rest on the injection run recorded in IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md §三 rather than on a resident test — reverting the regex to /new\s+Date/ is killed by no committed assertion, since src/tick.ts carries none of the three forbidden tokens. I verified statically what is verifiable: both guards now use /\bDate\b/ (test/tick.test.ts:51, test/s3.test.ts:263), which matches Date.now() where the old regex did not, and P1-P5 map onto the assertions the summary claims — P1 to C1, P2 to C3, P3 to C5a (non-degenerate: its input reaches zeroGrowthRounds 2 with proposed 0 and no cap hit), P4 to C6, P5 to both C8 and C9. C3 and C11 satisfy §8.1: each pairs two states differing in the asserted dimension and asserts the delta rather than two absolutes.
